response.passage: Motion is a change in an object's position over time. Every moving object possesses speed, regardless of whether it moves rapidly or crawls slowly. Speed is defined as the total distance covered divided by the total time taken to cover that distance. To calculate this correctly, ensure your units are consistent, such as kilometers per hour or meters per second, by converting minutes to hours if necessary. When we represent motion on a distance-time graph, a straight diagonal line indicates uniform motion, meaning the object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time. Conversely, a horizontal line on this graph signifies that the object is at rest, as the distance remains unchanged while time passes. In the study of periodic motion, a simple pendulum swings back and forth. One complete oscillation occurs when the bob moves from one extreme position to the other and returns to its starting point. Interestingly, the time period of a pendulum depends only on the length of the string, not on the mass of the bob or the width of the swing. A heavier bob or a wider swing does not change the time taken for one oscillation.
response.summary: Motion is measured by speed, which is calculated by dividing distance by time. Distance-time graphs help visualize motion, where horizontal lines show an object at rest. Pendulum swings are periodic, with their time period determined solely by string length.
